subject: Business Models
title: The Franchise Fee Structure
description: A quick win: understand The Franchise Fee Structure.

hook.text: Opening a McDonald's costs $1-2.2 million. The franchise fee is just $45,000 of that total.

buildup.text: Franchisees pay an upfront fee, ongoing royalties (4-8% of sales), and marketing fund contributions.

discovery.text: The franchise fee buys training and the right to use the brand. The real money is in ongoing royalties.

twist.text: Many franchisees discover that after royalties, rent, and labor, margins are razor-thin: 5-10% net profit.

climax.text: The franchisor's revenue is almost pure margin. Royalties flow in whether the franchisee is profitable or not.

punchline.text: $45,000 fee, $2.2 million total. The fee is just the beginning.

quiz.question: What is typically the largest ongoing cost for a franchisee?

details.summary: Franchise fee structures typically include an upfront franchise fee, ongoing royalties as a percentage of gross revenue, marketing fund contributions, and various operational fees. This layered revenue model means franchisors earn money regardless of whether individual franchisees are profitable.
details.whyItMatters: The fee structure reveals a fundamental tension in franchising: franchisors earn on gross revenue while franchisees earn on net profit..
takeaways: Franchisors charge upfront fees, ongoing royalties, and marketing contributions
Royalties are based on gross revenue, not profit, creating alignment gaps
Additional fees for technology, training, and supplies add to franchisee costs

faq.question: What are the main revenue streams for a franchisor?
faq.answer: Initial franchise fees for new locations, ongoing royalties typically 4 to 8 percent of gross revenue, national and local marketing fund contributions of 1 to 4 percent, technology system fees, supply chain markups, real estate income from owned locations, and training program fees.

faq.question: Why is the gross revenue royalty structure controversial?
faq.answer: Franchisors earn their percentage whether the franchisee is profitable or not. A store with 1 million in revenue and barely breaking even still pays 60,000 to 80,000 in royalties. This can push marginally profitable locations into losses while the franchisor continues earning.
